en.headline: CHAT opens Oh Haji first Hong Kong solo exhibition in Tsuen Wan
en.dek: The textile artist’s Becoming Flowers runs until 28 February at The Mills, exploring diasporic memory and female resilience through weaving, embroidery and dyeing.
body: CHAT, the Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile at The Mills in Tsuen Wan, opened three winter exhibitions on Saturday, including Oh Haji’s first solo show in Hong Kong.

Oh Haji: Becoming Flowers traces the artist’s use of textile materials and techniques to express diasporic memory, female resilience, communal healing and celebration. The flower motif runs through the works as a metaphor for cultural identity and strength amid displacement. Curated by CHAT’s executive director and chief curator Takahashi Mizuki, the exhibition brings together earlier pieces inspired by traditional dress with new community-created works.

The show runs from 14 November 2026 to 28 February 2027, daily from 11am to 7pm except Tuesdays when the venue is closed. Two companion exhibitions, Seed to Textile 2026: Costumes of Vivid Currents and Artefacts of Unravelling, open on the same dates. Admission is free.
Oh Haji, a third-generation Zainichi Korean born and raised in Japan, previously received the Audience Prize at the ANTEPRIMA x CHAT Contemporary Textile Art Prize 2024.

zh.headline: CHAT六廠荃灣開幕吳夏枝香港首個展
zh.dek: 紡織藝術家《花自漫生》展期至明年2月28日，於南豐紗廠透過編織、刺繡及染色探索離散記憶與女性韌性。
body: 荃灣南豐紗廠的CHAT六廠（六廠紡織文化藝術館）周六起推出三個冬季展覽，包括藝術家吳夏枝在香港的首次個人展覽。
《吳夏枝：花自漫生》回顧藝術家以紡織物料及技法表達離散記憶、女性韌性、社群療癒與慶祝的創作。花的意象貫穿作品，象徵文化身份及在離散中的內在力量。展覽由CHAT六廠執行董事及首席策展人高橋瑞木策劃，匯集早期以傳統服飾為靈感的作品及與香港社群共同創作的新作。
展覽由2026年11月14日至2027年2月28日，每日上午11時至晚上7時開放，逢星期二休館。同期開幕的另兩個展覽為《種學織文2026：霓裳絢流》及《拆解的痕跡》。入場免費。
吳夏枝是在日本出生及成長的第三代在日韓國人，曾於2024年ANTEPRIMA x CHAT六廠當代紡織藝術獎中獲得觀眾最喜愛大獎。
